concepts.name: 11-balanced-taper
concepts.description: Smaller rounding at all four tips, midway between 08 and the original.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Task: a very controlled refinement of the Flight Deck logo, intermediate between two supplied designs.
Image 1 is the chosen 08 Softened Compact logo, the primary EDIT TARGET. The user likes its shape but finds its rounded ends a little too round.
Image 2 is the earlier 04 Compact logo, a COMPARISON REFERENCE for the sharper boundary, not a design to copy exactly.
The output must have noticeably smaller end radii than image 1, but NO needle-sharp ends like image 2. Retain a tiny smoothly rounded finish at every tip. The narrowing should happen through longer tapered contours, not by clipping the ends flat. Think a tapered airfoil ending in a small smoothly radiused nose, rather than a rounded finger.
Preserve image 1's two black components, compact rising silhouette, upward diagonal sweep, the width and smooth curve of the white airflow channel, the lower-left banking turn, inward hooked tail, exact overall placement, white square background, and centered bold sans-serif wordmark "Flight Deck". Keep the lower curl's structure intact. No new concepts or major shape changes.
The FOUR terminals to refine are the uppermost upper-right tip, the second upper-right tip, the lower-left endpoint of the upper ribbon, and the right-facing endpoint of the lower curl.
Style: perfectly crisp flat solid black silhouettes on pure white. No gradients, shadows, texture, blur, bevels, or strokes. No added text or labels. One logo and one wordmark on this canvas. Preserve the wordmark exactly.
Variation: BALANCED TAPER. Reduce the visual radius of ALL FOUR terminal caps to approximately HALF that in image 1. Re-extend each tip gently along its existing direction and use a short convex fillet to join the tapering edges. At this 1254-pixel canvas scale, aim for a visible nose radius around 7–8 pixels rather than the source's much larger rounded cap. The upper-right ends should look elegantly tapered, with the last small part distinctly softened. The left endpoint and curled tail should be equally restrained. This is the middle ground between the two references, neither blunt nor razor-sharp. Do not merely reproduce image 1.

concepts.description: The most tapered option, with small rounded finishes.

Preserve image 1's two black components, compact rising silhouette, upward diagonal sweep, the width and smooth curve of the white airflow channel, the lower-left banking turn, inward hooked tail, exact overall placement, white square background, and centered bold sans-serif wordmark "Flight Deck".
